newsitem.title: TAIWAN: China's "Chiang Kai-shek" comes to Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China's "Chiang Kai-shek" comes to Taiwan.

text.p: An actor and look-alike for Taiwan's late Nationalist leader, Chiang Kai-shek, said on Thursday he came from China to Taiwan to fulfill his dream of seeing what the generalissimo had achieved.

Zhao Hengdo, famous in both China and Taiwan for playing the role of Chiang in a television series and movies, stunned journalists when he appeared at a news conference bearing a striking resemblance to Chiang.
Asked how he felt about coming to Taiwan, the 66-year-old Chinese actor said he was excited he could finally visit the island to see the legacy of the historic figure he has played for 19 years.
"Right after I stepped down the plane, I was excited," Zhao said.
He said he wanted to visit the shrine of the late Chiang in Taoyuan, northern Taiwan.
But Zhao, who planned to remain in Taiwan for 10 days, refrained from answering political questions.
On whether he thought Chiang was a national hero, Zhao cautiously said, "He was a historical figure."

Zhao said in 1949 when he first started his movie career in China, some of his friends told him that they saw his pictures hanging at some places in Nanjing. He only realised later that he looked like Chiang.

Chiang, who ruled China in the 1930s and 1940s, had set up a capital in Nanjing before his Nationalist government was driven off the mainland after losing a civil war to the Chinese communists in 1949.
Chiang later set up the Nationalist government in Taipei and ruled the island until he died on April 5, 1975.
Taiwan and China have remained bitter political rivals since the end of the civil war.
